ai.literal: Having known the assembly and having analyzed, let them speak, those of purity who have known the range of words.
ai.translation: Let those of pure character, who know the power and classification of words, speak only after assessing the nature of the assembly and analyzing their audience.
ai.modern: சொற்களின் தொகுதியை நன்கு அறிந்த தூய்மையான பண்புடையவர்கள், தாங்கள் பேசும் அவையின் தன்மையை அறிந்து, ஆராய்ந்து அதற்குப் பிறகு பேச வேண்டும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet outlines the prerequisite for effective public speaking. It addresses those of 'purity' (தூய்மையவர்), meaning people of flawless character and intellect who have mastered the vast range and classification of words (சொல்லின் தொகை அறிந்த). Even such experts must not speak hastily; they are advised to first understand the nature of the gathering (அவை அறிந்து) and carefully analyze the context (ஆராய்ந்து) before delivering their speech (சொல்லுக).

ai.literal: Having discerned the appropriate time, and having understood well, let them speak, those of goodness who have known the nature of speech.
ai.translation: Let those of good character, who know the nature of speech, discern the right opportunity and understand their audience thoroughly before they speak.
ai.modern: சொல்லின் தன்மையை அறிந்த நற்குணமுடையவர்கள், பேசுவதற்கு ஏற்ற நேரத்தை ஆராய்ந்து, அவையினரின் தன்மையை நன்றாக உணர்ந்து பேச வேண்டும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet highlights the essential qualities of effective communication. The poet advises that people of good character who understand the power and nature of words ('சொல்லின் நடை தெரிந்த நன்மையவர்') must speak with great care. They must first identify the right opportunity or timing ('இடை தெரிந்து') and then thoroughly comprehend the nature of their audience ('நன்கு உணர்ந்து'). Only when both the timing and the audience's disposition are favorable should they deliver their speech.

ai.literal: Those who do not know the assembly, those who undertake speaking, do not know the types of speech, and even that which they are skilled in does not exist.
ai.translation: Those who undertake to speak without understanding the nature of their audience do not comprehend the power of words; even the knowledge they are skilled in becomes utterly worthless.
ai.modern: அவையின் தன்மையை அறியாமல் பேசுதலைத் தொடங்குபவர்கள், சொற்களின் வகைகளை அறியாதவர்கள் ஆவர்; அவர்கள் கற்றறிந்த கல்வியும் பயனில்லாததாகிவிடும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet emphasizes the importance of understanding one's audience before speaking. Those who rush to speak without assessing the nature, intellect, and mood of the assembly (அவை) demonstrate a lack of understanding of the power and classification of words (சொல்லின் வகை). Even if they possess deep knowledge or skill (வல்லதூஉம்) in a particular subject, it becomes completely useless and non-existent (இல்) because it is delivered in an inappropriate forum. True eloquence requires not just subject knowledge, but also the wisdom to adapt it to the audience.

ai.literal: Before the intelligent, becoming intelligent; before the ignorant, assuming the color of white plaster.
ai.translation: Be highly intelligent in the presence of the wise; but before the ignorant, assume the blankness of white plaster.
ai.modern: அறிவுடையார் முன்னிலையில் தாமும் அறிவுடையவராக விளங்க வேண்டும்; அறிவில்லாதார் முன்னிலையில் வெண்மையான சுண்ணாம்புச் சாந்தின் நிறத்தைப் போலத் தாமும் ஒன்றும் அறியாதவர் போலக் காட்டிக் கொள்ள வேண்டும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet guides a speaker on how to adapt to different audiences. When standing before highly learned and intelligent people (ஒளியார்), one must shine with equal brilliance and display one's intellect (ஒள்ளியர் ஆதல்). However, when facing unlearned or ignorant people (வெளியார்), it is wise to blend in and appear completely blank or simple, like plain white plaster (வான்சுதை வண்ணம் கொளல்). Showing off deep wisdom to those who cannot comprehend it is useless and can cause unnecessary conflict, so adopting a simple, non-threatening demeanor is recommended.

ai.literal: Among those things said to be good, the best indeed is the restraint of not speaking before elders.
ai.translation: Among all things that are considered good, the restraint of not speaking before wise elders is indeed the best.
ai.modern: நன்மை என்று சொல்லப்பட்டவற்றுள்ளும் மிகச் சிறந்தது, அறிவு முதிர்ந்த பெரியோர்களுக்கு முன்னால் முந்திக்கொண்டு பேசாமல் அடங்கியிருக்கும் அடக்கமே ஆகும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet emphasizes the virtue of respectful silence and restraint in the presence of wise elders. The word 'முதுவர்' refers to those who are mature in both age and wisdom. 'முந்து கிளவாச் செறிவு' describes the self-control of not rushing to speak before these elders have spoken. The author declares that among all virtues considered good, this quiet deference is the most excellent.

ai.literal: Like slipping from a firm path is a slip of speech before those who accept and understand vast knowledge.
ai.translation: Making a slip of speech before those who can receive and understand vast knowledge is like losing one's footing and falling from a safe path.
ai.modern: பரந்த அறிவை ஏற்று ஆராயும் வல்லமை உடையவர்கள் முன்னிலையில், ஒருவர் பேசும்போது தவறு செய்வது என்பது, நல்ல வழியில் செல்லும்போது நிலை தடுமாறி விழுவதைப் போன்றதாகும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet emphasizes the gravity of making a mistake when speaking before an audience of highly learned and discerning scholars. The poet compares a slip of tongue or an error in argument before such an audience to a traveler losing their footing and falling while walking on a well-established path. Just as a fall on a smooth path is highly embarrassing and damaging, an intellectual slip before those who truly understand vast subjects ruins one's reputation instantly. Therefore, one must be extremely careful and precise when speaking in front of wise people.

ai.literal: The learning of those who have learned and understood will shine in the presence of those who are capable of analyzing words flawlessly.
ai.translation: The learning of those who have studied and understood will shine brilliantly when presented before those who are experts in analyzing words flawlessly.
ai.modern: நூல்களைக் கற்று அவற்றின் பொருளை உணர்ந்தவர்களுடைய கல்வியானது, சொற்களைக் குற்றமற ஆராய்ந்து அறியும் வல்லமை உடையவர்களின் அவையின்கண் விளங்கித் தோன்றும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet emphasizes the importance of the audience when expressing one's knowledge. The learning of a scholar only finds its true value and shines brightly when it is presented before an audience of experts who can flawlessly analyze and appreciate the nuances of language and argument. Speaking before those who cannot evaluate words is futile; it is the discerning assembly of critics and scholars that brings out the true luster of one's education. The key terms 'சொல்தெரிதல் வல்லார்' (those capable of analyzing words) and 'கசடற' (flawlessly) highlight that only a highly competent audience can truly validate and elevate a speaker's knowledge.

ai.literal: Speaking before those who possess understanding is like pouring water in the garden bed of that which grows.
ai.translation: Speaking before those who have the power of understanding is like pouring water into a garden bed of growing plants.
ai.modern: விளக்கிக் கூறும் அறிவை உடையவர்கள் முன்னிலையில் பேசுவது, வளரும் பயிர்கள் உள்ள பாத்தியில் நீர் ஊற்றுவதைப் போன்றது ஆகும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet compares speaking before an appreciative and understanding audience to watering a fertile garden bed where plants are already growing. When you speak to people who can truly comprehend and value your words, your ideas will take root, flourish, and yield great results, just as water helps growing crops thrive. The word 'உணர்வது உடையார்' refers to those who possess deep comprehension, and 'வளர்வதன் பாத்தி' represents a fertile, growing garden bed. This highlights the immense value of choosing the right audience for one's knowledge.

ai.literal: In the assembly of the ignorant, even by forgetfulness, do not speak, those who speak well so as to be received in the assembly of the wise.
ai.translation: Those who are capable of speaking in a wise assembly so that their words are well received should not, even by forgetfulness, speak in an assembly of the ignorant.
ai.modern: அறிவுடையோர் கூடியிருக்கும் நல்ல அவையில், கேட்பவர் மனதில் பதியும்படி நன்றாகப் பேச வல்லவர்கள், அறிவில்லாதவர்களின் புல்லவையில் மறந்தும் பேசக் கூடாது.
ai.explanation: This couplet advises skilled speakers on where to avoid speaking. Those who possess the rare talent of speaking effectively in an assembly of wise and noble people (நல்லவை) should never speak in an assembly of the ignorant or low-minded (புல்லவை), even by a slip of the mind or forgetfulness (பொச்சாந்தும்). The word 'சல' (often read as 'செல') means 'to go into' or 'to be received/understood' by the audience. Speaking to an audience that cannot appreciate or comprehend wisdom is futile and diminishes the speaker's value.

ai.literal: Holding a learned discourse before those who are not one's own peers is like nectar spilled inside a dirty drain.
ai.translation: Holding a learned discourse before those who are not one's peers is like spilling divine nectar into a dirty drain.
ai.modern: தம்முடைய அறிவுத் தரத்திற்குச் சமமில்லாதவர்கள் முன்னிலையில் அறிவார்ந்த சொற்பொழிவு ஆற்றுவது, சாக்கடையில் அமுதத்தைக் கொட்டுவதற்கு ஒப்பானதாகும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet highlights the importance of choosing the right audience for sharing high wisdom. The poet compares precious, refined knowledge to 'அமிழ்து' (divine nectar). Speaking such profound truths before 'தங்கணத்தார் அல்லார்' (those who are not one's intellectual peers) is a waste of effort. It is compared to spilling nectar into an 'அங்கணம்' (a dirty drain or sewer), where its purity and value are instantly ruined. Therefore, a wise person must only hold a discourse ('கோட்டி கொளல்') in an assembly of equals who can appreciate it.
